title: Returned Payment Charges on Assisted Living Accounts
content:
**Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement — payments returned unpaid by the bank.**

### Rule

One returned-payment charge is posted for each payment returned unpaid by the bank, referencing the entry that reinstated it, and it is the only charge that return carries. The charge is the returned payment fee for that return; once charged it appears on the resident's statement for the billing month given, and the amount owed on the residency account goes up by the fee.

Guest meals remain charged at the guest meal fee per meal, and the long-term care insurer direct billing administration fee remains charged monthly while direct billing of the insurer is in place.

### Charging the fee

The desk charges the returned payment fee with the agent-side tool `post_returned_payment_fee_036f277a`: the tool is first unlocked and then called by the agent. It writes one returned-payment add-on charge tied to the reinstated returned payment entry and dated the day it is charged; it does not look anything up or work out the amount.

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `assisted_residency_id` | Reference number of the assisted living residency charged, as returned by the assisted living residency lookup | Identifier |
| `source_entry_id` | Reference number of the ledger entry that reinstated the returned payment, as returned by the assisted living ledger lookup | Identifier |
| `billing_period` | The billing month the fee is charged in | YYYY-MM |
| `amount` | The fee in US dollars, positive, already rounded to the cent; it is charged exactly as given | Number with 2 decimal places |

### Return

On success the tool returns `status` "charged", `entry_id` (the reference number of the new fee charge), `source_entry_id` (the returned payment entry it refers to), `amount` (the USD fee, 2 decimal places) and `account_balance` (the residency balance in USD after the fee, 2 decimal places). The tool states no error return.

### Basis Q&A

**Which entry does the charge reference?** The ledger entry that reinstated the returned payment, not the original payment entry.

**Can one returned payment carry two returned-payment charges?** No; one charge is posted for each payment returned, and it is the only charge that return carries.
